title: Dec. 7 is the deadline for Pontotoc farms under USDA’s April drought designation
excerpt: Pontotoc was listed as a neighboring county eligible for emergency credit. A separate November notice gives other north Mississippi counties a July deadline.
locality: Pontotoc County and neighboring Lafayette and Union counties, Mississippi.

facts.statement: Pontotoc County farmers seeking emergency loans for losses covered by USDA’s April 22 drought designation have until Monday, Dec. 7, to apply. The Farm Service Agency named Pontotoc as a county adjoining a designated disaster area. Calhoun and Lafayette were among the 21 Mississippi counties listed as primary disaster areas.
facts.evidence: April notice explicitly lists Pontotoc under contiguous Mississippi counties, Calhoun and Lafayette under primary counties, and December 7 as deadline.
facts.date_context: April 22 and Nov. 16, 2026 notices, with separate deadlines Dec. 7, 2026 and July 6, 2027.
facts.locality: Pontotoc County and neighboring Lafayette and Union counties, Mississippi.
facts.identities: USDA Farm Service Agency and farm operators affected by the designated drought.

facts.statement: A second USDA notice issued Nov. 16 carries a later deadline that applies to a different group of counties. It names Alcorn, Benton, Marshall and Tippah as the primary counties and includes Lafayette and Union as neighbors. Pontotoc is absent from that notice, so its July 6, 2027, deadline does not extend the filing window under the April designation.
facts.evidence: Compared complete primary and contiguous lists and the deadlines in the two notices. No claim about other independent designations.

facts.statement: The loans can help replace essential equipment or livestock lost in a disaster. FSA reviews each application, including the operation’s losses, available collateral and ability to repay. Producers with questions about filing a notice of loss can select Mississippi and Pontotoc County in USDA’s service center locator to find the local office.

paragraphs.text: Pontotoc County farmers seeking emergency loans for losses covered by USDA’s April 22 drought designation have until Monday, Dec. 7, to apply. The Farm Service Agency named Pontotoc as a county adjoining a designated disaster area. Calhoun and Lafayette were among the 21 Mississippi counties listed as primary disaster areas.

A second USDA notice issued Nov. 16 carries a later deadline that applies to a different group of counties. It names Alcorn, Benton, Marshall and Tippah as the primary counties and includes Lafayette and Union as neighbors. Pontotoc is absent from that notice, so its July 6, 2027, deadline does not extend the filing window under the April designation.

The loans can help replace essential equipment or livestock lost in a disaster. FSA reviews each application, including the operation’s losses, available collateral and ability to repay. Producers with questions about filing a notice of loss can select Mississippi and Pontotoc County in USDA’s service center locator to find the local office.
